subject: Next steps: Novagen reserved pool + isolation checks
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@novagen.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novagen discovery — recap and proposed next steps (reserved pool + isolation)

Hey Sarah —

Great to chat this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so your team has a clean checklist to share with procurement/infra: 

Key pain points we heard
- Bursty inference traffic from model retrain windows causing 3–4x latency spikes during rollouts.
- Regulatory requirement to isolate PHI-related traffic to a private pool.
- Need predictable per-request latency for inference SLAs (p90 < 120ms) for patient-facing features.

Goals you outlined
- Lock in a dedicated GPU pool for inference (initial target: 8 GPU cards, ability to burst to 12).
- Tenant-level isolation for PHI workloads with audit logging and KMS integration.
- Two-week canary with fallback to hosted variants during peak deploy windows.

Proposed technical approach (high level)
1) Reserved pool: 8x A100-equivalent cards (dedicated) with burst scaling to 12.
2) Isolation: VPC peering + tenant-level routing and KMS for key management; audit log export to S3/GCS.
3) SLA targets: p90 inference latency target 120ms; availability SLA 99.9% for committed capacity.
4) Ops acceptance: run a 48-hour throughput soak with your model (we provide an ops checklist).

Attachments: I attached a short proposal (PDF) and an isolation checklist spreadsheet for your infra team.

Next steps
- Sarah: confirm whether Novagen prefers monthly or annual reservation pricing by EOD Thu (22 Jul).
- Novagen procurement: share standard PO template / payment timeline.
- Rishi/Ben/Laura: we’ll produce a one-page SOW + Ops Acceptance Criteria doc and route for signatures once you confirm term.

If useful I can schedule a 30-min follow-up with our infra engineer to walk the isolation checklist step-by-step — Ben can join.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Novagen discovery — recap and proposed next steps (reserved pool + isolation)

Thanks for the clear recap, Rishi — this matches what we discussed. A couple clarifying points from infra/procurement after a quick sync: 

- For the isolation design, we need explicit confirmation that we can route only PHI inference calls to the dedicated pool (i.e., no accidental cross-tenant co-mingling). Can Ben or Laura confirm the routing policy and TTL for KV cache isolation?
- Procurement asked if you have a standard term sheet for annual reservations and whether there are onboarding credits for an initial canary.
- For the SLA, our product team prefers a p95 latency commitment rather than p90; is that something Redwood can include in the SOW?

Tom (cc’d) is our infra lead — Tom, can you share the PO template and our internal timeline for procurement review (we’re aiming to approve by next Thursday 29th)?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Park
Head of ML Ops, Novagen
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@novagen.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 12:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novagen discovery — recap and proposed next steps (reserved pool + isolation)

Hi Sarah —

Quick answers: 
- Routing policy: we support request-level routing by tag. You can set the token that identifies PHI requests (example: header X-NVG-PHI: true) and traffic with that tag will be pinned to the dedicated pool. KV cache entries are namespace-isolated per pool; TTL is configurable (default 24h), but we can set to match your retention policy.
- p95 SLA: we can include a p95 latency target in the SOW for committed capacity; p95 <= 150ms is realistic with the sizing you asked for (we can fine-tune after benchmarks).
- Onboarding credits: we can offer a 2-week pilot credit (covers baseline compute for the canary) on annual reservations.

I’ve added an ops acceptance checklist (ops-acceptance-criteria.md) to the thread; it lists benchmarks we’ll run during the 48-hour soak and failure scenarios for the fallback.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) SOW & pricing: attached PDF includes annual vs monthly pricing and the 2-week pilot credit for annual.
2) Technical confirmations: Ben’s note above stands — request-level routing by header, KV cache namespace isolation, TTL configurable.
3) SLA language: we’ll include p95 <= 150ms for committed capacity in the SOW; fallback policy documented for degraded throughput.
4) Docs we’ll send to procurement: W-9, standard agreement (redlines accepted), and DocuSign SOW link once you confirm term.

Cheers,
Rishi
